prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1348; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection and described being struck from behind while stopped at a signal. Claimant stated neck pain and stiffness began within hours and was seen at a clinic the same day. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been cooperative so far.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle at the scene and records the rear impact as described. Two independent witnesses in the report give consistent accounts of the stop and the following vehicle's failure to slow.

Entry 3: Received photos from the claimant and the other driver showing rear-end damage to the claimant's vehicle. The damage pattern lines up with the impact described and with the force one would expect at this speed.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the collision happened as the claimant described it. The other driver's statement adds no detail that conflicts with the claimant's account.

Entry 5: Contacted the claimant to review the medical records from the initial clinic visit. Diagnosis is whiplash-type soft tissue injury, which is a typical outcome for a rear impact of this kind.

Entry 6: Checked the vehicle's history and found no prior damage on file. Repair estimate was reviewed and the listed repairs correspond to the damage in the photos.

Entry 7: Confirmed with the claimant's physician's office that treatment has followed a usual course, with physical therapy and then a taper as symptoms improved. Claimant's prior records show a minor strain in the same area years ago that resolved fully, which is noted and does not appear to be affecting the current claim.

Entry 8: Claimant's account has stayed the same across every call, email and recorded statement so far, including the timing of symptoms and the route taken that day.

Entry 9: Verified with the policy records that the driver involved is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates coverage.

Entry 10: Reviewed treatment progress with the claimant, who reports steady improvement and fewer missed days from work. Medical notes support the taper in visit frequency.

Entry 11: Claim is progressing normally. Liability appears clear, the injury and damage fit the accident, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation based on the documented treatment course.
